text:
sre-bot: PagerDuty alert: PAGER #3245 -> high p99 latency on /v1/generate-stream (canary v10 rollout) :rotating_light:

marta (oncall): i'm on it. can someone drop the immediate p95/p99 numbers + which region? paging the eng-platform folks.

leah (sre): seeing p95 ~ 220ms (ok) but p99 jumped to ~1.2s across us-west-2 and eu-west-1 since 2312349600. error budget burn flag tripped for streaming endpoints.

jason (eng-platform): confirmed spike correlates with canary traffic to model v10 that started at 2312349400. traffic split was 10% to v10, 90% v9. looks like v10 has a tail-slowpath for long context streaming.

marta (oncall): has anyone seen streaming stalls (clients stuck, no tokens) or just slow tokens?

leah (sre): both. lots of token dry spells for requests > 1k tokens. logs show repeated kv-cache misses and occasional gpu-spin stalls. stack traces point to decoder loop waiting on cross-shard KV lock.

jason (eng-platform): putting quick safeguarding steps: 1) reduce canary weight to 0% (switchback) 2) disable multiplexed streaming for canary model variants 3) throttle max-concurrency for long requests. propose commands below.

jason (eng-platform): run:```
# switch routing back to stable v9
redwoodctl routing update --model v10 --weight 0 --model v9 --weight 100 --reason "emergency switchback - p99 spike"
# disable multiplexing on v10 (safety)
redwoodctl model config set v10 --disable-multiplexing true
# apply short-term concurrency cap for streaming
redwoodctl route update /v1/generate-stream --max-concurrency 120
```

marta (oncall): executing now. will monitor.

ops: routing change applied at 2312349805. v10 weight -> 0. propagation should be immediate at edge but allow 30s for caches.

leah (sre): after switchback p99 dropped to ~210ms within 90s in us-west-2; eu-west-1 trending down. streaming stall rate reduced by ~95%. initial SLO breach window closed for p95/p99.

audrey (support): flagged two enterprise customers (org-872 and org-11) who reported intermittent stalls starting at ~2312349450. notified them about mitigation and that we're switching traffic back. drafting a message.

marta (oncall): good. what next on root cause? do we keep v10 disabled?

jason (eng-platform): we should mark v10 as quarantined for now. eng-runtime will reproduce with targeted load: long-context streaming and high fanout. next steps: 1) reproduce in staging with same batch/sequence distribution 2) gather GPU timelines and KV cache contention traces 3) test patch that avoids waiting on KV locks during decoding.

leah (sre): added Grafana panels + an alert for KV lock contention metric (kv.lock_wait_seconds) and a temporary runbook step to scale encoder pods if lock wait > 0.5s. query used:```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(kv_lock_wait_seconds_bucket[2m])) by (le))
```

marta (oncall): what's the customer impact summary for the incident report?

audrey (support): impact: ~3% of streaming requests experienced token stalls/p99 > 1s during the window. two enterprise customers had degraded UX (delayed completions, some retries). no permanent data loss. we offered priority support and provided timeline.

jason (eng-platform): decision log: rolled back v10 (switchback) at 2312349805. disabled multiplexing on v10, quarantined the model version. created follow-up ticket ENG-RT-1289 for KV-lock fix and regression tests.

leah (sre): postmortem tags: canary, rollout, p99, streaming-stall, kv-cache, switchback. recommend adding pre-rollout stress tests for long streaming contexts and enable canary circuit-breaker that auto-pauses canaries if streaming p99 > 800ms for 5m.

marta (oncall): handoff to morning oncall: @leah, please own postmortem and follow-ups. leaving notes in the incident doc.

sre-bot: Incident channel created -> #incidents/2312349876, severity: SEV2, incident lead: marta (oncall), runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-p99

marta (oncall): final status: mitigated via immediate switchback; customers notified; follow-up eng ticket open. handing to oncall tomorrow at 0800 PT. :white_check_mark:

audrey (support): will send closure emails and include timeline + mitigation steps.

jason (eng-platform): leaving a small post-rollback watch: I'll keep 15m cadence checks for next 2 hours and then move to 1h. I'll also coordinate a canary dry-run plan before reattempting v10.

leah (sre): note to self: attach heap traces + decoder wait stacks to ENG-RT-1289.

marta (oncall): thanks team. closing chat here, will update incident board.
